_**Kinsey**_ is a 2004 American [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") written and directed by [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-4) It describes the life of [Alfred Charles Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey") (played by [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson")), a pioneer in the area of [sexology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexology "Sexology"). His 1948 publication, _Sexual Behavior in the Human Male_ (the first of the [Kinsey Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Reports "Kinsey Reports")) was one of the first recorded works that tried to scientifically address and investigate [sexual behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexual_activity "Human sexual activity") in humans. The film also stars [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney") (in a performance nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress")), [Chris O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_O'Donnell "Chris O'Donnell"), [Peter Sarsgaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Sarsgaard "Peter Sarsgaard"), [Timothy Hutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Hutton "Timothy Hutton"), [John Lithgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lithgow "John Lithgow"), [Tim Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Curry "Tim Curry"), [Oliver Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Platt "Oliver Platt"), and [Dylan Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Baker "Dylan Baker").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kinsey_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Professor [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey") is interviewed about his sexual history. Interspersed with the interview are flashbacks from his childhood and young-adulthood. The early years show his father, a [lay minister of the Methodist church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodist_local_preacher "Methodist local preacher"), denouncing modern inventions as leading to sexual sin, then in early adolescence, humiliating Kinsey in a store by denouncing its keeper for showing him cigarettes, while his adolescence shows his experiences as a [Boy Scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Boy Scouts (Boy Scouts of America)") and a late teenage scene shows Kinsey disappointing his father by his chosen vocational intentions. The adult Kinsey teaches at [Indiana University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_University_Bloomington "Indiana University Bloomington") as a professor of biology lecturing on [gall wasps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gall_wasp "Gall wasp").

Kinsey falls in love with a student in his class, whom he calls [Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clara_McMillen "Clara McMillen"), and marries her. Consummation of their marriage is difficult at first, because of a medical problem Mac has that is fixed easily with minor surgery. At the university, Professor Kinsey, who is affectionately called "Prok" by his graduate students, meets with them after hours to offer individual sexual advice.

At a book party celebrating Kinsey's latest publication on gall wasps, Kinsey approaches the [dean of students](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_students "Dean of students") about an open-forum [sex education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_education "Sex education") course as opposed to the anti-sex propaganda taught in a general [health education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_education "Health education") class. It is approved, but on the grounds that it is open only to teachers, graduate or senior students, and married students. Kinsey begins teaching the sex course to a packed auditorium.

Kinsey continues answering students' questions in personal meetings but his answers are severely limited by the paucity of scientific data about human sexual behavior. This leads Kinsey to pass out questionnaires in his sexual education class from which he learns of the enormous disparity between what society had assumed people do and what their actual practices are. After securing financial support from the [Rockefeller Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation "Rockefeller Foundation"), Kinsey and his research assistants, including his closest assistant, [Clyde Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Martin "Clyde Martin"), travel the country, interviewing subjects about their sexual histories.

As time progresses Kinsey realizes that sexuality within humans, including himself, is a lot more varied than was originally thought. The range of expression he creates becomes known as the [Kinsey scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_scale "Kinsey scale"), which ranks overall sexuality from completely [heterosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterosexual "Heterosexual") to completely [homosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual").

The first sexological book Kinsey publishes, which is on the sexual habits of the male, is a large-scale success and a best seller. Kinsey turns his research to women and is met with more controversy. With the release of the volume on female sexual behavior, support for his work declines in a time when Senator [Joseph McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McCarthy "Joseph McCarthy")'s witch hunts against Communists and homosexuals (the latter known as the [Lavender Scare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavender_scare "Lavender scare")) lead the Rockefeller Foundation to withdraw its financial support, fearing that it be labeled "Communist" for backing the subversion of traditional [American values](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_values "American values").

Kinsey feels he has failed everyone who has ever been a victim of sexual ignorance. A customs officer is tipped off to an importation of some of Kinsey's research material, which only exacerbates the financial hardship of Kinsey's research organization. Kinsey suffers a heart attack, and is found to have developed an addiction to [barbiturates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbiturate "Barbiturate"). Meeting with other [philanthropists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philanthropy "Philanthropy") fails to garner the support needed. Still, Kinsey continues his taking of sex histories.

Returning to the initial interview, Kinsey is asked about love and whether he will ever conduct research on it. He responds that love is impossible to measure and impossible to quantify, but that it is important. Kinsey and Mac pull over to the side of the road for a nature walk. She remarks about a tree that has been there for a thousand years. Kinsey replies that the tree seems to display a strong love in the way its roots grip the earth. The two walk off together, Kinsey remarking "there's a lot of work to do".

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kinsey_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

Producer Gail Mutrux handed Bill Condon a biography of Kinsey in 1999 to spark his interest in writing a screenplay. Condon then based his original screenplay on elements in the biography combined with his own original research on Kinsey.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-hot-5)

[Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen") was at one point in negotiations for a supporting role.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-hot-5)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kinsey_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

_Kinsey_ was the first film permitted to show [human genitalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_organ "Sex organ") uncensored in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"), known for its strict censorship policies regarding genitalia.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-6)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kinsey_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

The [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") reported that 90% of critics have given the film a positive review based on 196 reviews, with an average rating of 7.66/10. The site's critics consensus reads, "A biopic of the sex researcher is hailed as adventurous, clever, and subversive, with fine performances by Liam Neeson and Laura Linney."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-7) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 79 out of 100 based on 40 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-8) Reviewing in the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_, [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") gave _Kinsey_ four out of four stars and hailed it as a "fascinating bio" whose strength lies in "the clarity it brings to its title character ... a complete original, a person of intelligence and extremes", as well as how it "captures its times, and a political and moral climate of fear and repression". Ebert compared Neeson's performance to that of [Russell Crowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Crowe "Russell Crowe") in the 2001 biopic _[A Beautiful Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Beautiful\_Mind "A Beautiful Mind")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-9)

The film grossed $10,254,979 domestically and $16,918,723 worldwide on an $11 million budget.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-mojo-3)

#### Let’s talk about sex

Kinsey is a portrait of researcher Alfred Kinsey, driven to uncover the most private secrets of a nation. What begins for Kinsey as a scientific endeavor soon takes on an intensely personal relevance, ultimately becoming an unexpected journey into the mystery of human behavior.

Then it was humans. Then sexual intercourse between humans. And then the diversity observable in the activity - which then became his life's work to chronicle.

_**Kinsey**_ is a 2004 American [biographical](link_20)[drama film](link_21) written and directed by [Bill Condon](link_3).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-4) It describes the life of [Alfred Charles Kinsey](link_22) (played by [Liam Neeson](link_5)), a pioneer in the area of [sexology](link_23). His 1948 publication, _Sexual Behavior in the Human Male_ (the first of the [Kinsey Reports](link_24)) was one of the first recorded works that tried to scientifically address and investigate [sexual behavior](link_25) in humans. The film also stars [Laura Linney](link_6) (in a performance nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](link_26)), [Chris O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_O [link_7]'Donnell "Chris O'Donnell"), [Peter Sarsgaard](link_8), [Timothy Hutton](link_9), [John Lithgow](link_10), [Tim Curry](link_11), [Oliver Platt](link_12), and [Dylan Baker](link_13).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kinsey_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Professor [Alfred Kinsey](link_22) is interviewed about his sexual history. Interspersed with the interview are flashbacks from his childhood and young-adulthood. The early years show his father, a [lay minister of the Methodist church](link_27), denouncing modern inventions as leading to sexual sin, then in early adolescence, humiliating Kinsey in a store by denouncing its keeper for showing him cigarettes, while his adolescence shows his experiences as a [Boy Scout](link_28) and a late teenage scene shows Kinsey disappointing his father by his chosen vocational intentions. The adult Kinsey teaches at [Indiana University](link_29) as a professor of biology lecturing on [gall wasps](link_30).

Kinsey falls in love with a student in his class, whom he calls [Mac](link_31), and marries her. Consummation of their marriage is difficult at first, because of a medical problem Mac has that is fixed easily with minor surgery. At the university, Professor Kinsey, who is affectionately called "Prok" by his graduate students, meets with them after hours to offer individual sexual advice.

At a book party celebrating Kinsey's latest publication on gall wasps, Kinsey approaches the [dean of students](link_32) about an open-forum [sex education](link_33) course as opposed to the anti-sex propaganda taught in a general [health education](link_34) class. It is approved, but on the grounds that it is open only to teachers, graduate or senior students, and married students. Kinsey begins teaching the sex course to a packed auditorium.

Kinsey continues answering students' questions in personal meetings but his answers are severely limited by the paucity of scientific data about human sexual behavior. This leads Kinsey to pass out questionnaires in his sexual education class from which he learns of the enormous disparity between what society had assumed people do and what their actual practices are. After securing financial support from the [Rockefeller Foundation](link_35), Kinsey and his research assistants, including his closest assistant, [Clyde Martin](link_36), travel the country, interviewing subjects about their sexual histories.

As time progresses Kinsey realizes that sexuality within humans, including himself, is a lot more varied than was originally thought. The range of expression he creates becomes known as the [Kinsey scale](link_37), which ranks overall sexuality from completely [heterosexual](link_38) to completely

American screenwriter and director

This article is about the director and screenwriter. For the Australian footballer, see [Bill Condon (footballer)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon_(footballer) "Bill Condon (footballer)").

**William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Condon&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Condon was born in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on October 22, 1955,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-ibdb-2) the son of a police [detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective "Detective"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-3) and was raised in an [Irish Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic "Irish Catholic") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-5) He attended [Regis High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(New_York_City) "Regis High School (New York City)") and [Columbia College of Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_of_Columbia_University "Columbia College of Columbia University"), graduating in 1976 with a degree in philosophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

Two films had a significant impact of Condon's early life. At the age of twelve, he found himself drawn to screenplay writing with his first viewing of [_Bonnie and Clyde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde_(film) "Bonnie and Clyde (film)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-6) In college he saw _[Sweet Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Charity\_(film) "Sweet Charity (film)")_ (1969), which led to "a lifelong love affair with movies that are reviled and rejected in their time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

After completing college, Condon worked as a journalist for film magazines, including _[American Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Film\_(magazine) "American Film (magazine)")_ and _Millimeter_. In 1981, he won "the world's most difficult film trivia quiz" sponsored by _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Condon&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

His career as a filmmaker began with screenplays for the [independent feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")_[Strange Behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Behavior "Strange Behavior")_ (1981), an homage to the pulp horror films of the 1950s,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-sb-8) and the [science-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science-fiction "Science-fiction") feature _[Strange Invaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Invaders "Strange Invaders")_ (1983), which starred [Nancy Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Allen_(actress) "Nancy Allen (actress)") and [Wallace Shawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Shawn "Wallace Shawn").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-9)

His directorial debut was _[Sister, Sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister,\_Sister\_(1987\_film) "Sister, Sister (1987 film)")_ (1987), an eerie [Southern Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Gothic "Southern Gothic") mystery starring [Eric Stoltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stoltz "Eric Stoltz") and [Jennifer Jason Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Jason_Leigh "Jennifer Jason Leigh"). Test screenings led to major changes to the film, which still proved a critical failure that set back Condon's career.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-10)

Condon emerged a few years later directing a series of made-for-TV thrillers, including _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(1991\_film) "Murder 101 (1991 film)")_ (1991), which earned Condon and co-writer Roy Johansen a 1992 [Edgar Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Award "Edgar Award") for their screenplay.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-mysterynet-11) During this period he also wrote the screenplay for the thriller _[F/X2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/X2 "F/X2")_ (1991), which was directed by Australian director [Richard Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Franklin_(director) "Richard Franklin (director)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-12)

In 1994, he directed the television movie _[The Man Who Wouldn't Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_Who\_Wouldn't\_Die\_(1995\_film) "The Man Who Wouldn't Die (1995 film)"),_ which was met with mixed reviews.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-13) He directed _[Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candyman:\_Farewell\_to\_the\_Flesh "Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh")_ (1995), a sequel to [Bernard Rose's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Rose_(director) "Bernard Rose (director)") 1992 horror film. It was a critical and commercial failure.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-14) Reminded years later of this phase of his career, Condon said: "It's hard to be lower on the totem pole than being the director for a sequel to a horror movie."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

Condon wrote and directed _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_ (1998), which was based on a novel by [Christopher Bram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Bram "Christopher Bram"). His screenplay won the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay"). _The New York Times_ said Condon "may have been the most stunned person at the Academy Awards when his name was announced as the winner for the best adapted screenplay. He has struggled for years in Hollywood as a screenwriter and journalist and is unaccustomed to the hoopla that is now around him."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-15) He was nominated for the same award for his screenplay for _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, based on the Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(musical) "Chicago (musical)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-16) He received a second Edgar Award for his _Chicago_ screenplay as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-17)

In 2004 he wrote and directed the film _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, chronicling the life of the controversial sex researcher [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey"). In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." He continued: "I can't think of another movie that has dealt with sex so knowledgeably and, at the same time, made the pursuit of knowledge seem so sexy. There are some explicit images and provocative scenes, but it is your intellect that is most likely to be aroused.... Mr. Condon's great achievement is to turn Kinsey's complicated and controversial career into a grand intellectual drama."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-18)

In 2005, he received the [Stephen F. Kolzak Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Awards "GLAAD Media Awards") at the [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") Media Awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-19)

Condon wrote the screenplay for and directed _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, an adaptation of the acclaimed Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls "Dreamgirls"). It was released in December 2006. Condon received [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominations for directing. The film was nominated for eight Academy Awards in six categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-20)

Condon was executive producer of the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") television broadcast that aired on February 22, 2009, working with producer [Laurence Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Mark "Laurence Mark").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-21)

Condon directed both parts of _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Dawn\_(disambiguation) "Breaking Dawn (disambiguation)")_ (2011 and 2012), adapted from the fourth and final novel in _[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(novel\_series) "Twilight (novel series)")_ by [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer"). He was twice nominated for a [Razzie for Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director") for these films, winning for _Part 2_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-22)

Condon directed _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ (2013), a thriller about [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") starring [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch"). He said he chose the project for a change of pace and liked its non-ideological approach to a very complex subject. He saw it "in the great tradition of journalistic thrillers".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-23) It received mixed responses from critics and underperformed at the box office.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-24)

In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)

In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)

Condon directed the 2017 [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures")'s [live action film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_and_the_Beast_(2017_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)"), [based on](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_remakes_and_adaptations_of_Disney_animated_films "List of remakes and adaptations of Disney animated films") the animated 1991 film _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(1991\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)")_, starring [Emma Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Watson "Emma Watson") and [Dan Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Stevens "Dan Stevens").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) A few weeks before the film's scheduled release on March 17, 2017, Condon announced that one character, LeFou, has "a nice, exclusively gay moment", which resulted in an "internet meltdown" of contrasting support and condemnation.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-28)

He co-authored the screenplay for _[The Greatest Showman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Greatest\_Showman "The Greatest Showman")_, a biography of [P.T. Barnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P.T._Barnum "P.T. Barnum"), starring [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") and released in December 2017. He rewrote the draft of co-author [Jenny Bicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_Bicks "Jenny Bicks").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-29)

In October 2017, Condon postponed pre-production of a remake of _[Bride of Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride\_of\_Frankenstein#Remake\_attempts "Bride of Frankenstein")_ for [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ reported that Condon and [David Koepp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp "David Koepp") wanted to rework the script.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-30)

Condon is a member of the Independent Feature Projects (IFP) in Los Angeles, a non-profit organization which supports independent films, as well as the Independent Writers Steering Committee, which was initiated by the Writers Guild of America (WGA).

In July 2021, Condon signed on to direct a _[Guys and Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guys\_and\_Dolls "Guys and Dolls")_ movie adaptation by [TriStar Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TriStar_Pictures "TriStar Pictures") but left the project in 2023 and was replaced by _Chicago_ director [Rob Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Marshall "Rob Marshall").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-31) That same year, he co-produced the [live stage filming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_from_Away_(film) "Come from Away (film)") of the Broadway production of _[Come from Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_from\_Away "Come from Away")_, which was released to streaming on [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-32)

In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)

In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Condon&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)

In [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film "Film") and [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_show "Television show"), **drama** is a category or genre of [narrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrative "Narrative")[fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiction "Fiction") (or [semi-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docudrama "Docudrama")) intended to be more serious than [humorous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humour "Humour") in tone.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-1) The drama of this kind is usually qualified with additional terms that specify its particular super-genre, macro-genre, or micro-genre,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2) such as [soap opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap_opera "Soap opera"), [police crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_procedural "Police procedural"), [political drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_drama "Political drama"), [legal drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_drama "Legal drama"), [historical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama"), [domestic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_drama "Domestic drama"), [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#Teen_drama), and [comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama") (dramedy). These terms tend to indicate a particular [setting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Setting_(narrative) "Setting (narrative)") or subject matter, or they combine a drama's otherwise serious tone with elements that encourage a broader range of [moods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_(literature) "Mood (literature)"). To these ends, a primary element in a drama is the occurrence of [conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict_(process) "Conflict (process)")—emotional, social, or otherwise—and its resolution in the course of the storyline.

All forms of [cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_industry "Film industry") or television that involve [fictional stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiction "Fiction") are forms of [drama in the broader sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama "Drama") if their storytelling is achieved by means of actors who [represent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representation_(arts) "Representation (arts)") ([mimesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimesis "Mimesis")) [characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_(arts) "Character (arts)"). In this broader sense, drama is a [mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_(literature) "Mode (literature)") distinct from novels, [short stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_story "Short story"), and narrative [poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poetry "Poetry") or [songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song "Song").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-elam98-3) In the [modern era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_era "Modern era"), before the birth of cinema or television, "drama" within [theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre "Theatre") was a type of [play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_(theatre) "Play (theatre)") that was neither a [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_(drama) "Comedy (drama)") nor a [tragedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragedy "Tragedy"). It is this narrower sense that the film and television industries, along with [film studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_studies "Film studies"), adopted. "[Radio drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_drama "Radio drama")" has been used in both senses—originally transmitted in a live performance, it has also been used to describe the more [highbrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highbrow "Highbrow") and serious end of the dramatic output of [radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio "Radio").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-4)

## Types of drama in film and television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Types of drama in film and television")]

The [Screenwriters Taxonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriters_Taxonomy "Screenwriters Taxonomy") contends that film genres are fundamentally based upon a film's atmosphere, character and story, and therefore the labels "drama" and "comedy" are too broad to be considered a genre.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2) Instead, the taxonomy contends that film dramas are a "Type" of film; listing at least ten different sub-types of film and television drama.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017b-5)

### Docudrama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Docudrama")]

Main article: [Docudrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docudrama "Docudrama")

Docudramas are dramatized adaptations of real-life events. While not always completely accurate, the general facts are more-or-less true.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-6) The difference between a docudrama and a documentary is that in a documentary it uses real people to describe history or current events; in a docudrama it uses professionally trained actors to play the roles in the current event, that is "dramatized" a bit. Examples: _[Black Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mass\_(film) "Black Mass (film)")_ (2015) and _[Zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac\_(film) "Zodiac (film)")_ (2007).

### Docufiction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Docufiction")]

Main article: [Docufiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docufiction "Docufiction")

Unlike docudramas, docu-fictional films combine documentary and fiction, where actual footage or real events are intermingled with recreated scenes.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-7) Examples: _[Interior. Leather Bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interior.\_Leather\_Bar. "Interior. Leather Bar.")_ (2013) and _[Your Name Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your\_Name\_Here\_(2015\_film) "Your Name Here (2015 film)")_ (2015).

### Comedy drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Comedy drama")]

Main article: [Comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")

Many otherwise serious productions have humorous scenes and characters intended to provide [comic relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_relief "Comic relief"). A comedy drama has humor as a more central component of the story, along with serious content.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-8)Examples include _[Three Colours: White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three\_Colours:\_White "Three Colours: White")_ (1994), _[The Truman Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Truman\_Show "The Truman Show")_ (1998), _[The Man Without a Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_Without\_a\_Past "The Man Without a Past")_ (2002), _[The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Best\_Exotic\_Marigold\_Hotel "The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel")_ (2011), and _[Silver Linings Playbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver\_Linings\_Playbook "Silver Linings Playbook")_ (2012).

### Hypardrama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Hypardrama")]

Coined by film professor Ken Dancyger, these stories exaggerate characters and situations to the point of becoming fable, legend or fairy tale.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-9)Examples: _[Fantastic Mr. Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantastic\_Mr.\_Fox\_(film) "Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)")_ (2009) and _[Maleficent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maleficent\_(film) "Maleficent (film)")_ (2014).

### Light drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Light drama")]

Light dramas are light-hearted stories that are, nevertheless, serious in nature.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-10)Examples: _[The Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Help\_(film) "The Help (film)")_ (2011) and _[The Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Terminal "The Terminal")_ (2004).

### Psychological drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Psychological drama")]

Main article: [Psychological drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_drama "Psychological drama")

Psychological dramas are dramas that focus on the characters' inner life and psychological problems.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-11) Examples: _[Requiem for a Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Requiem\_for\_a\_Dream "Requiem for a Dream")_ (2000), _[Oldboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldboy\_(2003\_film) "Oldboy (2003 film)")_ (2003), _[Babel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babel\_(2006\_film) "Babel (2006 film)")_ (2006), _[Whiplash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiplash\_(2014\_film) "Whiplash (2014 film)")_ (2014), and _[Anomalisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomalisa "Anomalisa")_ (2015).

### Satirical drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Satirical drama")]

See also: [Satire (film and television)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)")

Satire can involve humor, but the result is typically sharp social commentary that is anything but funny. Satire often uses irony or exaggeration to expose faults in society or individuals that influence social ideology.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2019-12)Examples: _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking "Thank You for Smoking")_ (2005) and _[Idiocracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiocracy "Idiocracy")_ (2006).

### Straight drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Straight drama")]

Straight drama applies to those that do not attempt a specific approach to drama but, rather, consider drama as a lack of comedic techniques.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2019-12)Examples: _[Ghost World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_World\_(film) "Ghost World (film)")_ (2001) and _[Wuthering Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuthering\_Heights\_(2011\_film) "Wuthering Heights (2011 film)")_ (2011).

### Tragedy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Tragedy")]

Like most [tragedies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragedy "Tragedy") in early [theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre "Theatre"), Tragedy typically focuses on the downfall or suffering of a main character (or sometimes supporting characters) due to a series of unfortunate events, often culminating in their demise at the end of the film or television series. Examples: _[The Elephant Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Elephant\_Man\_(1980\_film) "The Elephant Man (1980 film)")_ (1980), _[Grave of the Fireflies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave\_of\_the\_Fireflies "Grave of the Fireflies")_ (1988), _[The Green Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Green\_Mile\_(film) "The Green Mile (film)")_ (1999), _[The Mist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mist\_(film) "The Mist (film)")_ (2007), and _[The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boy\_in\_the\_Striped\_Pyjamas\_(film) "The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas (film)")_ (2008).

## Type/genre combinations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Type/genre combinations")]

According to the Screenwriters' Taxonomy, all film descriptions should contain their type (comedy or drama) combined with one (or more) of the eleven super-genres.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2) This combination does not create a separate genre, but rather, provides a better understanding of the film.

According to the taxonomy, combining the type with the genre does not create a separate genre.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2) For instance, the "Horror Drama" is simply a dramatic horror film (as opposed to a comedic horror film). "Horror Drama" is not a genre separate from the horror genre or the drama type.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-13)

### Crime drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Crime drama")]

Crime dramas explore themes of truth, justice, and freedom, and contain the fundamental dichotomy of "criminal vs. lawman". Crime films make the audience jump through a series of mental "hoops"; it is not uncommon for the crime drama to use verbal gymnastics to keep the audience and the protagonist on their toes.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2)Crime dramas often include settings like the scene of the crime, the police station, forensic labs, and in some cases, courts of law.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-14) This feeds into the drama, and it adds senses of character to the film.

Examples of crime dramas include: _[The Godfather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Godfather "The Godfather")_ (1972), _[Chinatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown\_(1974\_film) "Chinatown (1974 film)")_ (1974), _[Goodfellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas "Goodfellas")_ (1990), _[The Usual Suspects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Usual\_Suspects "The Usual Suspects")_ (1995), and _[The Big Short](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Short\_(film) "The Big Short (film)")_ (2015).

### Fantasy drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Fantasy drama ")]

According to [Eric R. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_R._Williams "Eric R. Williams"), the hallmark of fantasy drama films is "a sense of wonderment, typically played out in a visually intense world inhabited by mythic creatures, magic or superhuman characters.Props and costumes within these films often belie a sense of mythology and folklore – whether ancient, futuristic, or other-worldly. The costumes, as well as the exotic world, reflect the personal, inner struggles that the hero faces in the story."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2)

Examples of fantasy dramas include _[The Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lord\_of\_the\_Rings\_(film\_series) "The Lord of the Rings (film series)")_ (2001–2003), _[Pan's Labyrinth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan's\_Labyrinth "Pan's Labyrinth")_ (2006), _[Where the Wild Things Are](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where\_the\_Wild\_Things\_Are\_(film) "Where the Wild Things Are (film)")_ (2009), and _[Life of Pi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_of\_Pi\_(film) "Life of Pi (film)")_ (2012).

### Horror drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Horror drama ")]

Horror dramas often involve the central characters isolated from the rest of society. These characters are often teenagers or people in their early twenties (the genre's central audience) and are eventually killed off during the course of the film. Thematically, horror films often serve as morality tales, with the killer serving up violent penance for the victims' past sins.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017b-5)Metaphorically, these become battles of Good vs. Evil or Purity vs. Sin.

_[Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycho\_(1960\_film) "Psycho (1960 film)")_ (1960), _[The Shining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shining\_(film) "The Shining (film)")_ (1980), _[The Conjuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Conjuring "The Conjuring")_ (2013), _[It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_(2017\_film) "It (2017 film)")_ (2017), _[mother!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother! "Mother!")_ (2017), and _[Hereditary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereditary\_(film) "Hereditary (film)")_ (2018) are examples of horror drama films.

### Life drama (day-in-the-life)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Life drama (day-in-the-life)")]

Further information: [Slice of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slice_of_life "Slice of life")

Day-in-the-life films takes small events in a person's life and raises their level of importance.The "small things in life" feel as important to the protagonist (and the audience) as the climactic battle in an action film, or the final shootout in a western.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017b-5)Often, the protagonists deal with multiple, overlapping issues in the course of the film – just as we do in life.

Films of this type/genre combination include: _[The Wrestler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrestler\_(2008\_film) "The Wrestler (2008 film)")_ (2008), _[Fruitvale Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruitvale\_Station "Fruitvale Station")_ (2013), _[Locke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locke\_(film) "Locke (film)")_ (2013), _[The Great Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Beauty "The Great Beauty")_ (2013) and _[The Last Beautiful Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Beautiful\_Thing "The Last Beautiful Thing")_ (2025).

### Romantic drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Romantic drama")]

Romantic dramas are films with central themes that reinforce our beliefs about love (e.g.: themes such as "love at first sight", "love conquers all", or "there is someone out there for everyone"); the story typically revolves around characters falling into (and out of, and back into) love.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-15) Romantic drama often involves two characters who go through various trials and tribulations together as their relationship grows over time.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-16) often times there is a conflict between the two characters, which results in a temporary separation, but they often come back together for an optimistic ending.

_[Annie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie\_Hall "Annie Hall")_ (1977), _[The Notebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Notebook "The Notebook")_ (2004), _[Carol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol\_(film) "Carol (film)")_ (2015), _[Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her\_(2013\_film) "Her (2013 film)")_ (2013)_, [The Great Gatsby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Gatsby\_(2013\_film) "The Great Gatsby (2013 film)")_ (2013) _and [La La Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_La\_Land "La La Land")_ (2016) are examples of romance dramas.

### Science fiction drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Science fiction drama")]

The science fiction drama film is often the story of a protagonist (and their allies) facing something "unknown" that has the potential to change the future of humanity; this unknown may be represented by a villain with incomprehensible powers, a creature we do not understand, or a scientific scenario that threatens to change the world; the science fiction story forces the audience to consider the nature of human beings, the confines of time or space or the concepts of human existence in general.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-17)

Examples include: _[Metropolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis\_(1927\_film) "Metropolis (1927 film)")_ (1927), _[Planet of the Apes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet\_of\_the\_Apes\_(1968\_film) "Planet of the Apes (1968 film)")_ (1968), _[A Clockwork Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Clockwork\_Orange\_(film) "A Clockwork Orange (film)")_ (1971), _[Blade Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_Runner "Blade Runner")_ (1982) and its sequel _[Blade Runner 2049](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_Runner\_2049 "Blade Runner 2049")_ (2017), _[Children of Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_Men "Children of Men")_ (2006), _[Interstellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstellar\_(film) "Interstellar (film)")_ (2014), and _[Arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrival\_(film) "Arrival (film)")_ (2016).

### Sports drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Sports drama")]

Further information: [Sports film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_film "Sports film")

In the sports super-genre, characters will be playing sports. Thematically, the story is often one of "Our Team" versus "Their Team"; their team will always try to win, and our team will show the world that they deserve recognition or redemption; the story does not always have to involve a team. The story could also be about an individual athlete or the story could focus on an individual playing on a team.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-18)

Examples of this genre/type include:_[The Hustler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hustler "The Hustler")_ (1961), _[Hoosiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoosiers\_(film) "Hoosiers (film)")_ (1986), _[Remember the Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remember\_the\_Titans "Remember the Titans")_ (2000), and _[Moneyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneyball\_(film) "Moneyball (film)")_ (2011).

### War drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: War drama")]

Further information: [War film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film")

War films typically tell the story of a small group of isolated individuals who – one by one – get killed (literally or metaphorically) by an outside force until there is a final fight to the death; the idea of the protagonists facing death is a central expectation in a war drama film. In a war film even though the enemy may out-number, or out-power, the hero, we assume that the enemy _can_ be defeated if only the hero can figure out how.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017b-5)

Examples include: _[Apocalypse Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apocalypse\_Now "Apocalypse Now")_ (1979), _[Come and See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_and\_See "Come and See")_ (1985), _[Braveheart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braveheart "Braveheart")_ (1995), _[Life Is Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_Is\_Beautiful "Life Is Beautiful")_ (1997), _[Black Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Book\_(film) "Black Book (film)")_ (2006), _[The Hurt Locker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hurt\_Locker "The Hurt Locker")_ (2008), _[1944](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944\_(film) "1944 (film)")_ (2015), _[Wildeye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildeye "Wildeye")_ (2015), and _[1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1917\_(2019\_film) "1917 (2019 film)")_ (2019).

### Western drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Western drama ")]

Films in the [western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") super-genre often take place in the [American Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Southwest "American Southwest") or Mexico, with a large number of scenes occurring outdoors so we can soak in scenic landscapes.Visceral expectations for the audience include fistfights, gunplay, and chase scenes.There is also the expectation of spectacular panoramic images of the countryside including sunsets, wide open landscapes, and endless deserts and sky.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2)

Examples of western dramas include: _[True Grit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Grit\_(1969\_film) "True Grit (1969 film)")_ (1969) and its [2010 remake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_Grit_(2010_film) "True Grit (2010 film)"), _[Mad Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Max\_(film) "Mad Max (film)")_ (1979), _[Unforgiven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unforgiven "Unforgiven")_ (1992), _[No Country for Old Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Country\_for\_Old\_Men "No Country for Old Men")_ (2007), _[Django Unchained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Django\_Unchained "Django Unchained")_ (2012), _[Hell or High Water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell\_or\_High\_Water\_(film) "Hell or High Water (film)")_ (2016), and _[Logan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan\_(film) "Logan (film)")_ (2017).

## Misidentified categories

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Misidentified categories")]

Some film categories that use the word "comedy" or "drama" are not recognized by the Screenwriters Taxonomy as either a film genre or a film type.For instance, "Melodrama" and "Screwball Comedy" are considered pathways,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-19)while "romantic comedy" and "family drama" are macro-genres.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-20)

### Family drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Family drama")]

A macro-genre in the Screenwriters Taxonomy. These films tell a story in which many of the central characters are related.The story revolves around how the family as a whole reacts to a central challenge. There are four micro-genres for the family drama: _Family Bond_, _Family Feud_, _Family Loss_, and _Family Rift_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-Williams2017a-2)

### Melodrama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Melodrama")]

Main article: [Melodrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melodrama "Melodrama")

A sub-type of drama films that uses plots that appeal to the heightened emotions of the audience. Melodramatic plots often deal with "crises of human emotion, failed romance or friendship, strained familial situations, tragedy, illness, neuroses, or emotional and physical hardship".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-21) Film critics sometimes use the term "pejoratively to connote an unrealistic, pathos-filled, [camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_(style) "Camp (style)") tale of romance or domestic situations with stereotypical characters (often including a central female character) that would directly appeal to feminine audiences".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)#cite_note-22) Also called "women's movies", "weepies", tearjerkers, or "chick flicks". If they are targeted to a male audience, then they are called "guy cry" films. Often considered "soap-opera" drama.

### Liturgical drama / religious drama / Christian drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Liturgical drama / religious drama / Christian drama")]

See also: [Liturgical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liturgical_drama "Liturgical drama") and [Christian drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_drama "Christian drama")

Focuses on religious characters, mystery play, beliefs, and respect.

### Crime drama / police procedural / legal drama / courtroom drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Crime drama / police procedural / legal drama / courtroom drama")]

See also: [Crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama"), [police procedural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_procedural "Police procedural"), and [legal drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_drama "Legal drama")

Character development based on themes involving criminals, law enforcement and the legal system.

### Historical drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Historical drama")]

Main article: [Historical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")

Films that focus on dramatic events in history.

### Medical drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Medical drama")]

Main article: [Medical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_drama "Medical drama")

Focuses on doctors, nurses, hospital staff, and ambulance saving victims and the interactions of their daily lives.

### Teen drama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Drama_(film_and_television)&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Teen drama")]

See also: [List of teen dramas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_teen_dramas "List of teen dramas")

Focuses on [teenage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage "Teenage") characters.

**Alfred Charles Kinsey** ([/ˈ k ɪ n z i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); June 23, 1894 – August 25, 1956) was an American [sexologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexologist "Sexologist"), [biologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biologist "Biologist"), and professor of [entomology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entomology "Entomology") and [zoology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology "Zoology") who, in 1947, founded the Institute for Sex Research at [Indiana University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_University_Bloomington "Indiana University Bloomington"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-1) now known as the [Kinsey Institute for Research in Sex, Gender, and Reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Institute_for_Research_in_Sex,_Gender,_and_Reproduction "Kinsey Institute for Research in Sex, Gender, and Reproduction"). He is best known for writing _Sexual Behavior in the Human Male_ (1948) and _Sexual Behavior in the Human Female_ (1953), also known as the [Kinsey Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Reports "Kinsey Reports"), as well as for the [Kinsey scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_scale "Kinsey scale"). Kinsey's research on [human sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexuality "Human sexuality"), foundational to the field of [sexology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexology "Sexology"), provoked controversy in the 1940s and 1950s, and has continued to provoke controversy decades after his death.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-4) His work has influenced social and cultural values in the United States and United Kingdom as well as internationally.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alfred_Kinsey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Alfred Kinsey was born on June 23, 1894, in [Hoboken, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey "Hoboken, New Jersey"), the son of Sarah Ann ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Charles) and Alfred Seguine Kinsey.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-Timeline-5) He was the eldest of three children. His mother received little formal education; his father was a professor at [Stevens Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevens_Institute_of_Technology "Stevens Institute of Technology").

Kinsey's parents were devout Christians. His father was known as one of the most devout members of the local [Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodism "Methodism") church. Most of Kinsey's social interactions were with other members of the church, often as a silent observer, while his parents discussed religion.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-6) Kinsey's father imposed strict rules on the household, including mandating Sunday as a day of prayer and little else.

Kinsey's parents were poor for most of his childhood, often unable to afford proper medical care. This may have led to a young Kinsey receiving inadequate treatment for a variety of diseases including [rickets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickets "Rickets"), [rheumatic fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheumatic_fever "Rheumatic fever"), and [typhoid fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid_fever "Typhoid fever"). His health records indicate that Kinsey received suboptimal exposure to sunlight (often the cause of rickets, before milk and other foods were fortified with [vitamin D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_D "Vitamin D")) and lived in unsanitary conditions for at least part of his childhood. Rickets led to a curvature of the spine, which resulted in a slight stoop that prevented Kinsey from being [drafted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Draft "The Draft") in 1917 for [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I").

At age 10, Kinsey moved with his family to [South Orange, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Orange,_New_Jersey "South Orange, New Jersey").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-Timeline-5) Also at a young age, he showed great interest in nature and camping. He worked and camped with the local [YMCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YMCA "YMCA") throughout his early years, and enjoyed these activities to such an extent that he intended to work for the YMCA after completing his education. Kinsey's senior undergraduate thesis for psychology, a dissertation on the [group dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_dynamics "Group dynamics") of young boys, echoed this interest. He joined the [Boy Scouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America") when a troop was formed in his community. His parents strongly supported this (and joined as well) because the Boy Scouts was an organization that was based on the principles of Christianity. Kinsey worked his way up through the Scouting ranks to earn [Eagle Scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_Scout_rank_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Eagle Scout rank (Boy Scouts of America)") in 1913, making him one of the earliest Eagle Scouts.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-7) Despite earlier disease having weakened his heart, Kinsey followed an intense sequence of difficult hikes and camping expeditions throughout his early life.

In high school, Kinsey was a quiet but hard-working student. While attending [Columbia High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_High_School_(New_Jersey) "Columbia High School (New Jersey)"), he devoted his energy to academic work and playing the piano. At one time, Kinsey had hoped to become a concert pianist, but decided to concentrate on his scientific pursuits instead. Kinsey's ability to spend immense amounts of time deeply focused on study was a trait that would serve him well in college and during his professional career. He seems not to have formed strong social relationships during high school, but earned respect for his academic ability. While there, Kinsey became interested in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology "Biology"), [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany "Botany") and [zoology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology "Zoology"). Kinsey was later to claim that his high school biology teacher, Natalie Roeth, was the most important influence on his decision to become a scientist.

Kinsey approached his father with plans to study botany at college. His father demanded that he study engineering at [Stevens Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevens_Institute_of_Technology "Stevens Institute of Technology") instead. At Stevens, he primarily took courses related to English and engineering, but was unable to satisfy his interest in biology. Kinsey was not successful there, and decided engineering was not a field at which he could excel. At the end of two years at Stevens, Kinsey gathered the courage to confront his father about his interest in biology and his intent to continue studying at [Bowdoin College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowdoin_College "Bowdoin College") in Brunswick, Maine, where he majored in biology.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-8)

## Initial research on entomology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alfred_Kinsey&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Initial research on entomology")]

See also: [Category:Taxa named by Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Taxa_named_by_Alfred_Kinsey "Category:Taxa named by Alfred Kinsey")

In the fall of 1914, Kinsey entered Bowdoin College, where he studied [entomology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entomology "Entomology") under Manton Copeland, and was admitted to the [Zeta Psi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeta_Psi "Zeta Psi") fraternity, in whose house he lived for much of his time at college.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-10) In 1916 Kinsey was elected to the [Phi Beta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa "Phi Beta Kappa") society and graduated [magna cum laude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_cum_laude "Magna cum laude"), with degrees in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology "Biology") and [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-11) Alfred Seguine Kinsey did not attend his son's graduation ceremony at Bowdoin, possibly as another sign of disapproval of his son's choice of career and studies.

Kinsey continued his graduate studies at [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University")'s [Bussey Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bussey_Institute "Bussey Institute"), which had one of the most highly regarded biology programs in the United States. It was there that Kinsey studied applied biology under [William Morton Wheeler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morton_Wheeler "William Morton Wheeler"), a scientist who made outstanding contributions to [entomology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entomology "Entomology"). Under Wheeler, Kinsey worked almost completely autonomously, which suited both men quite well.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Atrusca_brevipennata_imported_from_iNaturalist_photo_177598458_on_25_October_2023.jpg/250px-Atrusca_brevipennata_imported_from_iNaturalist_photo_177598458_on_25_October_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Atrusca_brevipennata_imported_from_iNaturalist_photo_177598458_on_25_October_2023.jpg)

[Oak-apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_apple "Oak apple") galls induced by _[Atrusca brevipennata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrusca\_brevipennata "Atrusca brevipennata")_, one of the wasp species first described by Kinsey

Kinsey wrote his doctoral thesis on [gall wasps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gall_wasp "Gall wasp"), zealously collecting samples of the species. He traveled widely and took 26 detailed measurements of hundreds of thousands of gall wasps; his methodology was itself an important contribution to entomology as a science. In 1919, Kinsey was awarded an [Sc.D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Science "Doctor of Science") from [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"), and he accepted an academic post in biology at Indiana University. In 1920 he published several papers under the auspices of the [American Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Museum_of_Natural_History "American Museum of Natural History") in New York City, introducing the gall wasp to the scientific community and describing its [phylogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogeny "Phylogeny"). Of the more than 18 million insects in the museum's collection, some 5 million are gall wasps collected by Kinsey.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-12)

Kinsey wrote a widely used high-school textbook, _An Introduction to Biology_, which was published in October 1926.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-14) The book endorsed [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") and unified, at the introductory level, the previously separate fields of zoology and botany.

> _An Introduction to Biology_ was unlike any other textbook on the market... Kinsey's textbook was noteworthy for the strong position it took on evolution... In his textbook Kinsey laid out the basic facts of evolution in a manner-of-fact matter, as though he were discussing the life cycle of the fruit fly.... The chapter called "Further Evidence of Change" was especially blunt... Kinsey defined evolution as "the scientific word for change", and while he acknowledged that there are some people who "think they don't believe in evolution", he tried to show his students the folly of such reasoning. To find proof of evolution, students had only to look at things they used daily... Kinsey ridiculed the man who denounced evolution but owned a new breed of dog or smoked a cigar made from a recently improved variety of tobacco, saying, "When he says he doesn't believe in evolution, I wonder what he means."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-15)

Kinsey co-authored _Edible Wild Plants of Eastern North America_, published in 1943, with [Merritt Lyndon Fernald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merritt_Lyndon_Fernald "Merritt Lyndon Fernald"). The original draft of the book was written in 1919–1920, while Kinsey was still a doctoral student at the Bussey Institute, and Fernald was working at the [Arnold Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Arboretum "Arnold Arboretum").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey#cite_note-16)

## Sexology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alfred_Kinsey&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sexology")]

### The Kinsey Reports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alfred_Kinsey&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Kinsey Reports")]

Main article: [Kinsey Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Reports "Kinsey Reports")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Front_row_%28left_to_right%29-_Cornelia_V._Christenson%3B_Mrs._Leser%3B_Clyde_E._Martin._Arranged_on_steps_%28left_to_right%29-_Mrs._Brown%3B_Paul_H._Gebhard%3B_William_Dellenback%3B_Alfred_E._Kinsey%3B_Wardell_B._%285493916199%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Front_row_(left_to_right)-_Cornelia_V._Christenson;_Mrs._Leser;_Clyde_E._Martin._Arranged_on_steps_(left_to_right)-_Mrs._Brown;_Paul_H._Gebhard;_William_Dellenback;_Alfred_E._Kinsey;_Wardell_B._(5493916199).jpg)

Kinsey (center) with staff of the Institute for Sexual Research, later renamed the [Kinsey Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Institute "Kinsey Institute")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Alfred_Kinsey-TIME-1953.jpg/250px-Alfred_Kinsey-TIME-1953.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alfred_Kinsey-TIME-1953.jpg)
