The **Most Excellent Order of the British Empire** is a British [order of chivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_chivalry "Order of chivalry"), rewarding valuable service in a wide range of useful activities.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-obe_royal-2) It comprises six classes of appointments across both civil and [military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Armed_Forces "British Armed Forces") divisions, the most senior two of which make the recipient either a [knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders,_decorations,_and_medals_of_the_United_Kingdom#Modern_honours "Orders, decorations, and medals of the United Kingdom") if male or a [dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame_(title) "Dame (title)") if female.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1917-3)

The order was established on 4 June 1917 by King [George V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_V "George V"), who created the order to recognise "such persons, male or female, as may have rendered or shall hereafter render important services to [Our Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1917-3) Equal recognition was to be given for services rendered in the UK and overseas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4) The order was retained after the [decline of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire#Decolonisation_and_decline_(1945%E2%80%931997) "British Empire") in the second half of the 20th century. The majority of recipients are UK citizens, though a number of [Commonwealth realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm") outside the UK continue to make appointments to the order.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Commonwealth-5) Honorary appointments may be made to citizens of other nations of which the order's sovereign is not the head of state.

Appointments are announced in _[The Gazette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_London\_Gazette "The London Gazette")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-6)

## Classes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Classes")]

The six classes of appointment to the order are, from highest to lowest:

1.   Knight [Grand Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Cross "Grand Cross") or [Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame "Dame") Grand Cross of the Order of the British Empire (GBE);[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-7)
2.   [Knight Commander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Commander "Knight Commander") or Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (KBE or DBE);
3.   Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE);
4.   Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE);
5.   Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE);
6.   Recipient of the [British Empire Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire_Medal "British Empire Medal") (BEM).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-centralchancery.org.uk-8)

The two highest ranks, Knight or Dame Grand Cross and Knight or Dame Commander, entitle the holder to use the title Sir or Dame before their forename, except in the case of honorary appointments.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-thegazette.co.uk-9)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

King [George V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_V "George V") founded the order to fill gaps in the [British honours system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders,_decorations,_and_medals_of_the_United_Kingdom "Orders, decorations, and medals of the United Kingdom"):[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-thegazette.co.uk-9)

*   The Orders of the [Garter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Garter "Order of the Garter"), the [Thistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Thistle "Order of the Thistle") and [St Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_Patrick "Order of St Patrick") honoured royals, peers, statesmen and eminent military commanders;
*   The [Order of the Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Bath "Order of the Bath") honoured senior military officers and civil servants;
*   The [Order of St Michael and St George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_Michael_and_St_George "Order of St Michael and St George") honoured diplomats and colonial officials;
*   The [Order of the Star of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Star_of_India "Order of the Star of India") and the [Order of the Indian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Indian_Empire "Order of the Indian Empire") honoured Indian rulers and British and Indian officials of the [British Indian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Indian_Empire "British Indian Empire"); and
*   The [Royal Victorian Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Victorian_Order "Royal Victorian Order"), in the personal gift of the monarch, honoured those who had personally served the royal family.

In particular, George V wished to create an order to honour the many thousands of individuals from across the Empire who had served in a variety of non-combat roles during the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-obe_royal-2)

From its foundation the order consisted of five classes (GBE, KBE/DBE, CBE, OBE and MBE) and was open to both men and women; provision was also made for conferring honorary appointments on foreign recipients.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1917-3) At the same time, alongside the order, the Medal of the Order of the British Empire was instituted, to serve as a lower appointment granting recipients affiliation but not membership. The first investiture took place at [Ibrox Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibrox_Stadium "Ibrox Stadium"), as part of a royal visit to the Glasgow shipyards, with the appointment of [Alexander Ure, 1st Baron Strathclyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Ure,_1st_Baron_Strathclyde "Alexander Ure, 1st Baron Strathclyde") as a GBE (in recognition of his role as chairman of the Scottish War Savings Committee) and the conferral of medal of the order to Lizzie Robinson, a munitions worker.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory1-10)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/MBE-Cobh-Heritage-Centre-2012.JPG/250px-MBE-Cobh-Heritage-Centre-2012.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MBE-Cobh-Heritage-Centre-2012.JPG)

MBE (civil division) as issued in 1918

The order had been established primarily as being for civilians; in August 1918, however, not long after its foundation, a number of appointments were made to serving naval and military personnel. Four months later, a 'Military Division' was added to the order, to which serving personnel would in future be appointed.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-11) The classes were the same as for the Civil Division (as it was now termed), but military awards were distinguished by the addition of a central vertical red stripe to the purple riband of the civil awards. In 1920, appointment as an MBE "for an act of gallantry" was granted for the first time, to Sydney Frank Blanck Esq, who had rescued an injured man from a burning building containing explosives.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory1-10)

In December 1922, the statutes of the order were amended; there having been a large number of awards for war work prior to this date, these amended statutes placed the order on more of a peacetime footing.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4) For the first time numbers of appointments were limited, with the stipulation that senior awards in the Civil Division were to outnumber those in the Military Division by a proportion of six to one.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1922-12) Furthermore appointments in the civil division were to be divided equally between UK and overseas awards.

With regard to the Medal of the Order (but not the order itself), a distinction was made in 1922 between awards "for gallantry" and awards "for meritorious service" (each being appropriately inscribed, and the former having laurel leaves decorating the clasp, the latter oak leaves).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1922-12) In 1933, holders of the medal "for gallantry", which had come to be known as the [Empire Gallantry Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Gallantry_Medal "Empire Gallantry Medal"), were given permission to use the postnominal letters EGM (and at the same time to add a laurel branch emblem to the ribbon of the medal); however, in 1940, awards of the EGM ceased and all holders of the medal were instructed to exchange it for a new and more prestigious gallantry award: the [George Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Cross "George Cross").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13) In 1941, the medal of the order "for meritorious service" was renamed the [British Empire Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire_Medal "British Empire Medal"), and the following year its recipients were granted the right to use the postnominal letters BEM.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4) During the war, the BEM came to be used to recognise acts of bravery which did not merit the conferral of the George Cross or the [George Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Medal "George Medal"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13) a use which continued until the introduction of the [Queen's Gallantry Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Gallantry_Medal "Queen's Gallantry Medal") in 1974.

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Order_of_the_British_Empire_Insignia.jpg/250px-Order_of_the_British_Empire_Insignia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Order_of_the_British_Empire_Insignia.jpg)

Examples of insignia of the order (1937 pattern). Top to bottom: KBE or CBE (military) badge and riband, GBE star, KBE/DBE star, MBE (civil) and OBE (military) badges and ribands.

The designs of insignia of the order and medal were altered in 1937, prior to the [coronation of King George VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_of_King_George_VI "Coronation of King George VI"), 'in commemoration of the reign of King George V and Queen Mary, during which the Order was founded'.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4) The figure of [Britannia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia "Britannia") at the centre of the badge of the order was replaced with an image of the crowned heads of the late King and Queen Mary, and the words 'Instituted by King George V' were added to the reverse of the medal. The colour of the [riband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riband "Riband") was also changed: twenty years earlier, prior to the order's establishment, Queen [Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_of_Teck "Mary of Teck") had made it known that pink would be her preferred colour for the riband of the proposed new order, but, in the event, purple was chosen.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Galloway1996-14) Following her appointment as [Grand Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_master_(order) "Grand master (order)") of the order in 1936 a change was duly made and since 9 March 1937 the riband of the order has been 'rose pink edged with pearl grey' (with the addition of a vertical pearl grey stripe in the centre for awards in the military division).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-15)

From time to time the order was expanded: there was an increase in the maximum permitted number of recipients in 1933, and a further increase in 1937. During the Second World War, as had been the case during and after World War I, the number of military awards was greatly increased; between 1939 and 1946 there were more than 33,000 appointments to the Military Division of the order from the UK and across the Empire.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13) Recommendations for all appointments to the Order of the British Empire were originally made on the nomination of the King's United Kingdom ministers (recommendations for overseas awards were made by the [Foreign Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Office "Foreign Office"), the [Colonial Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Office "Colonial Office"), the [India Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Office "India Office") and the [Dominions Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominions_Office "Dominions Office")); but in the early 1940s the system was changed to enable the governments of overseas dominions to make their own nominations; Canada and [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_South_Africa "Union of South Africa") began doing so in 1942, followed by Australia, New Zealand and other Commonwealth realms.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13)

In May 1957, forty years after the foundation of the order, it was announced that [St Paul's Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul's_Cathedral "St Paul's Cathedral") was to serve as the church of the order, and in 1960 a chapel was dedicated for its use within the [crypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crypt "Crypt") of the cathedral.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13) That year, [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") awards made up 40% of all OBEs and MBEs appointed (and 35% of all living recipients of the higher awards).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory4-16) Gradually that proportion reduced as independent states within the Commonwealth established their own [systems of honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders,_decorations,_and_medals_of_the_Commonwealth_realms "Orders, decorations, and medals of the Commonwealth realms"). The last Canadian recommendation for the Order of the British Empire was an MBE for gallantry [gazetted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_London_Gazette "The London Gazette") in 1966, a year before the creation of the [Order of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Canada "Order of Canada"). On the other hand, the [Australian Honours System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Honours_System "Australian Honours System") unilaterally created in 1975 did not achieve bi-partisan support until 1992, which was when Australian federal and state governments agreed to cease Australian recommendations for British honours; the last Australian recommended Order of the British Empire appointments were in the [1989 Queen's Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Birthday_Honours "1989 Birthday Honours"). New Zealand continued to use the order alongside [its own honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_royal_honours_system "New Zealand royal honours system") until the establishment of the [New Zealand Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Order_of_Merit "New Zealand Order of Merit") in 1996.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-17) Other Commonwealth realms have continued to use the Order of the British Empire alongside their own honours.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Commonwealth-5)

In 1993, the Prime Minister, [John Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Major "John Major"), instituted a [reform of the honours system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders,_decorations,_and_medals_of_the_United_Kingdom#Reform "Orders, decorations, and medals of the United Kingdom") with the aim 'that exceptional service or achievement will be more widely recognised; that greater importance will be given to voluntary service; that automatic honours will end; that the distinction between ranks in military operational gallantry awards will cease'.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-18) The reforms affected the order at various levels: for example the automatic appointment each year of a GBE to the [Lord Mayor of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Mayor_of_London "Lord Mayor of London") ceased; appointment as OBE replaced the [Imperial Service Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Service_Order "Imperial Service Order") for civil servants, and the number of MBEs appointed each year was significantly increased. As part of these reforms, the British Empire Medal stopped being awarded by the United Kingdom;[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-19) those who would formerly have met the criteria for the medal were instead made eligible for appointment as MBE.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory5-20)

In 2004, a report entitled _A Matter of Honour: Reforming Our Honours System_ by a [Commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom "House of Commons of the United Kingdom")[select committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Select_committee_(United_Kingdom) "Select committee (United Kingdom)") recommended phasing out the Order of the British Empire, as its title was "now considered to be unacceptable, being thought to embody values that are no longer shared by many of the country's population".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-21) The committee further suggested changing the name of the order to the Order of British Excellence, and changing the rank of Commander to Companion (as the former was said to have a "militaristic ring"), as well as advocating for the abolition of knighthoods and damehoods;[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-23) the government, however, was not of the opinion that a case for change had been made, and the aforementioned suggestions and recommendations were not, therefore, pursued.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory5-20)

In the 21st century quotas were introduced to ensure consistent representation among recipients across nine categories of eligibility:

*   Arts and media
*   Community, voluntary and local
*   Economy
*   Education
*   Health
*   Parliamentary and political
*   Science and technology
*   Sport
*   State

with the largest proportion of awards being reserved for community, voluntary and local service.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory5-20)

Non-military awards of the British Empire Medal resumed in 2012, starting with 293 BEMs awarded for [Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-24)

In 2017, the centenary of the order was celebrated with a service at St Paul's Cathedral.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory5-20)

## Composition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Composition")]

The order is limited to 300 Knights and Dames Grand Cross, 845 Knights and Dames Commander, and 8,960 Commanders. There are no limits applied to the total number of members of the fourth and fifth classes, but no more than 858 officers and 1,464 members may be appointed per year. Foreign appointees, as honorary members, do not contribute to the numbers restricted to the order as full members do. Although the Order of the British Empire has by far the highest number of members of the British orders of chivalry, with more than 100,000 living members worldwide, there are fewer appointments to knighthoods than in other orders.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-obe_royal-2)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-25)

From time to time, individuals may be promoted to a higher grade within the Order, thereby ceasing usage of the junior post-nominal letters.

### Sovereign and Grand Master

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Sovereign and Grand Master")]

The second-most senior officer is the [Grand Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Master_(order) "Grand Master (order)") (a 'Prince of the Blood Royal, or other exalted personage' appointed by the sovereign, who, by virtue of their appointment, becomes 'the First or Principal Knight Grand Cross of the same Order').[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1917-3)

### Officers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Officers")]

Not to be confused with [Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Most_Excellent_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire").

In addition to the sovereign and the [grand master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_master_(order) "Grand master (order)"), the order has six officers:[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-26)

*   Prelate: [Bishop of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_of_London "Bishop of London"), _vacant_
*   Dean: [Dean of St Paul's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_St_Paul's "Dean of St Paul's") (_[ex officio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex\_officio "Ex officio")_), The Very Rev. [Andrew Tremlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Tremlett "Andrew Tremlett")
*   Secretary: Secretary of the [Central Chancery of the Orders of Knighthood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Chancery_of_the_Orders_of_Knighthood "Central Chancery of the Orders of Knighthood"), Lieutenant Colonel Stephen Segrave
*   Registrar: [Secretary of the Cabinet and Head of the Civil Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_Secretary_(United_Kingdom) "Cabinet Secretary (United Kingdom)"), Dame [Antonia Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonia_Romeo "Antonia Romeo")[DCB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame_Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_Bath "Dame Commander of the Order of the Bath")
*   [King of Arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Arms_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "King of Arms of the Order of the British Empire"): Lieutenant General Sir [Simon Mayall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Mayall "Simon Mayall")[KBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire")[CB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_of_the_Order_of_the_Bath "Companion of the Order of the Bath")[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-27)
*   [Lady Usher of the Purple Rod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Usher_of_the_Purple_Rod "Lady Usher of the Purple Rod"): Dame [Amelia Fawcett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Fawcett "Amelia Fawcett")[DBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame_Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire")[CVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_Royal_Victorian_Order "Commander of the Royal Victorian Order")

At its foundation the order was served by three officers: the King of Arms, the Registrar & Secretary and the Gentleman Usher of the Purple Rod. In 1922, the Prelate was added, and the office of Registrar was separated from that of Secretary: the former was to be responsible for recording all proceedings connected with the order, issuing warrants under the seal of the order and making arrangements for investitures, while the latter (at that time the [Permanent Secretary to the Treasury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_Secretary_to_the_Treasury "Permanent Secretary to the Treasury")) was responsible for collecting and tabulating the names of those who were to receive an award.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1922-12) The office of Dean was added in 1957.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory3-13)

The King of Arms is not a member of the [College of Arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Arms "College of Arms"), as are many other [heraldic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heraldry "Heraldry") officers; and the Lady Usher of the Purple Rod does not – unlike the [Order of the Garter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Garter "Order of the Garter") equivalent, the Gentleman Usher of the [Black Rod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Rod "Black Rod") – perform any duties related to the [House of Lords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Lords "House of Lords").

Since the Second World War, several [Commonwealth realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm") have established their own national system of honours and awards and have created their own unique orders, decorations and medals.

Following the creation of the [Order of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Australia "Order of Australia") in 1975, the Government of the [Commonwealth of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Australia "Commonwealth of Australia") ceased finally to make recommendations for the Order of the British Empire in 1983, though various Australian state governments continued to make recommendations up to the [1989 New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_New_Year_Honours "1989 New Year Honours").

The Government of [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") ceased to make recommendations to the Order of the British Empire with the creation of the [New Zealand Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Order_of_Merit "New Zealand Order of Merit") in 1996.

A number of Commonwealth realms and territories continue to make recommendations for appointments to the Order of the British Empire. Most members of the order are citizens of the United Kingdom or other Commonwealth realms that use the UK system of honours and awards. In addition, honorary awards may be made to citizens of nations where the monarch is not [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"); these permit use of post-nominal letters, but not the title of _Sir_ or _Dame_. Honorary appointees who later become a citizen of a Commonwealth realm can convert their appointment from honorary to substantive, and they then enjoy all privileges of membership of the order, including use of the title of _Sir_ and _Dame_ for the senior two ranks of the Order.

## Gallantry awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Gallantry awards")]

[![Image 15: A crossed pair of oak leaves, in silver, against a background of red woven ribbon material](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Order_of_the_British_Empire_for_gallantry%2C_oak_leaves_ribbon_emblem.jpg/250px-Order_of_the_British_Empire_for_gallantry%2C_oak_leaves_ribbon_emblem.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Order_of_the_British_Empire_for_gallantry,_oak_leaves_ribbon_emblem.jpg)

A silver oak-leaf emblem denoted an appointment made "for gallantry" between 1958 and 1974.

Although initially intended to recognise meritorious service, the order began to also be awarded for gallantry. There were an increased number of cases in the Second World War for service personnel and civilians including the merchant navy, police, emergency services and civil defence, mostly MBEs but with a small number of OBEs and CBEs. Such awards were for gallantry that did not reach the standard of the [George Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Medal "George Medal") (even though, as appointments to an order of chivalry, they were listed before it on the [Order of Wear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_honours_order_of_wearing "United Kingdom honours order of wearing")). In contrast to awards for meritorious service, which usually appear without a citation, there were often citations for gallantry awards, some detailed and graphic.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-29) From 14 January 1958, these awards were designated Commander, Officer or Member of the Order of the British Empire for Gallantry.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-LG1958-30)

Any individual made a member of the order for gallantry after 14 January 1958 wears an emblem of two crossed silver oak leaves on the same ribbon as the badge, with a miniature version on the ribbon bar when worn alone. When the ribbon only is worn the emblem is worn in miniature.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-LG1958-30) It could not be awarded [posthumously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posthumous_award "Posthumous award"), and was replaced in 1974 with the [Queen's Gallantry Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Gallantry_Medal "Queen's Gallantry Medal") (QGM). If recipients of the Order of the British Empire for Gallantry received promotion within the order, whether for gallantry or otherwise, they continued to wear also the insignia of the lower grade with the oak leaves;[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-31) however, they used only the post-nominal letters of the higher grade.

When the order was founded in 1917, badges, ribands and stars were appointed for wear by recipients. In 1929, mantles, hats and collars were added for recipients of the highest class of the order (GBE). The designs of all these items underwent major changes in 1937.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Galloway1996-14)

### Badge

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Badge")]

The badge is worn by all members of the order; the size, colour and design depends on the class of award. The badge for all classes is in the form of a _cross [patonce](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/patonce "wikt:patonce")_ (having the arms growing broader and floriated toward the end) with a medallion in the centre, the obverse of which bears a crowned image of [George V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_V "George V") and Queen [Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_of_Teck "Mary of Teck") within a circlet bearing the motto of the Order; the reverse bears George V's Royal and Imperial Cypher. (Prior to 1937 [Britannia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia "Britannia") was shown within the circlet.) The size of the badges varies according to rank: the higher classes have slightly larger badges. The badges of Knights and Dames Grand Cross, Knights and Dames Commander, and Commanders are enamelled, with pale blue crosses, crimson circlets and a gold central medallion. Officers' badges are plain silver-gilt, while those of Members are plain silver.

### Riband

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Riband")]

From 1917 until 1937, the badge of the order was suspended on a purple ribbon, with a red central stripe being added for the military division in 1918. Since 1937, the ribbon has been rose-pink with pearl-grey edges (with the addition of a pearl-grey central stripe for the military division). Knights and Dames Grand Cross wear it on a broad riband or sash, passing from the right shoulder to the left hip. Knights Commander and male Commanders wear the badge from a ribbon around the neck; male Officers and Members wear the badge from a ribbon on the left chest; female recipients other than Dames Grand Cross (unless in military uniform) normally wear it from a bow on the left shoulder.

### Star

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Star")]

An oval eight-pointed star is worn, pinned to the left breast, by Knights and Dames Grand Cross; Knights and Dames Commander wear a smaller star composed of "four equal points and four lesser".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Gazette1917-3) The star is not worn by the more junior classes. Prior to 1937 each star had in the centre a gold medallion with a figure of Britannia, surrounded by a crimson [circlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circlet "Circlet") inscribed with the motto of the order ("For God and the Empire"); since 1937, the effigies of King George V and Queen Mary have been shown within the circlet.

### Mantles and collars

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mantles and collars")]

In 1929, to bring the order into line with the other orders of chivalry, members of the first class of the order (GBE) were provided with mantles, hats and collars.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentenaryHistory2-4)

*   The _mantle_ is a cloak-like garment of rose-pink satin lined with pearl-grey silk (prior to 1937 it was of purple satin). On the left side is a representation of the star of the order (as pictured below).
*   Initially a purple plumed hat was also provided to be worn with the mantle; in 1937, the colour of the hat was changed to black.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Galloway1996-14)
*   The _collar_ is made of gold. It consists of six medallions depicting the Royal Arms, alternating with six medallions depicting the Royal and Imperial Cypher of George V (_GRI_, which stands for "_\_Georgius Rex Imperator\__"). The medallions are linked with gold cables depicting '[sea-lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea-lion "Sea-lion")' and crowns. When collars are worn the badge is suspended from the collar.

Only Knights/Dames Grand Cross wear these elaborate vestments; the hat is now rarely, if ever, worn. Use of the mantle is limited to important occasions (such as quadrennial services and [coronations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_of_the_British_monarch "Coronation of the British monarch")). The mantle is always worn with the collar. Although the mantle was introduced in 1929, very few mantles would have been produced prior to the 1937 design changes, as there were few occasions for wearing them in the intervening years.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Galloway1996-14)

On certain days designated by the sovereign, known as "[collar days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collar_day "Collar day")", members attending formal events may wear the order's collar over their military uniform, formal day dress, evening wear or robes of office.

Collars are returned upon the death of their owners, but other insignia may be retained.

The six office-holders of the order wear pearl-grey silk mantles lined with rose-pink satin, having on the right side a purple shield charged with the roundel from the badge.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-CentySvc-32) Each of these office-holders wears a unique badge of office, suspended from a gold chain worn around the neck.

The _British Empire Medal_ is made of silver. On the obverse is an image of Britannia surrounded by the motto, with the words "For Meritorious Service" at the bottom; on the reverse is George V's Imperial and Royal Cypher, with the words "Instituted by King George V" at the bottom. The name of the recipient is engraved on the rim. It comes in both full-sized and miniature versions – the latter for formal white-tie and semi-formal black-tie occasions.

A [lapel pin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Award_pin "Award pin") for everyday wear was first announced at the end of December 2006, and is available to recipients of all levels of the order, as well as to holders of the [British Empire Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire_Medal "British Empire Medal"). The pin design is not unique to any level. The pin features the badge of the order, enclosed in a circle of ribbon of its colours of pink and grey. Lapel pins must be purchased separately by a member of the order.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-33) The creation of such a pin was recommended in Sir [Hayden Phillips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayden_Phillips "Hayden Phillips")' review of the honours system in 2004.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-34)

## Chapel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Chapel")]

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/St-Pauls-Cathedral_London_Crypta_Chapel-Order-Of-The-British-Empire-01.jpg/250px-St-Pauls-Cathedral_London_Crypta_Chapel-Order-Of-The-British-Empire-01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St-Pauls-Cathedral_London_Crypta_Chapel-Order-Of-The-British-Empire-01.jpg)

Chapel of the Order in the [crypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crypt "Crypt") of [St Paul's Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul's_Cathedral "St Paul's Cathedral") (photographed in 2013). The banners are those of the _Sovereign_ (right) and of the _Grand Master_ (left) of the Order as they were then in office.

The Chapel of the Order of the British Empire is in [St Paul's Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul's_Cathedral "St Paul's Cathedral"). It occupies the far eastern end of the cathedral crypt and was dedicated in 1960. The only heraldic banners normally on display in the chapel are those of the _Sovereign of the Order of the British Empire_ and of the _Grand Master of the Order of the British Empire_. Rather than using this chapel, the Order now holds its great services upstairs in the nave of the cathedral. In addition to the Chapel of the Order of the British Empire, St Paul's Cathedral also houses the Chapel of the [Order of St Michael and St George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_Michael_and_St_George "Order of St Michael and St George"). Religious services for the whole Order are held every four years; new Knights and Dames Grand Cross are installed at these services.

## Precedence and privileges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Precedence and privileges")]

See also: [Order of precedence in England and Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_precedence_in_England_and_Wales "Order of precedence in England and Wales")

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Order_of_the_British_Empire_-_Non_Arms.svg/250px-Order_of_the_British_Empire_-_Non_Arms.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Order_of_the_British_Empire_-_Non_Arms.svg)

Knights, Dames and Commanders of the Order may display its [circlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circlet "Circlet") around (and suspend its [Badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heraldic_badge "Heraldic badge") below) their [coat of arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms").

Knights Grand Cross and Knights Commander prefix _Sir_, and Dames Grand Cross and Dames Commander prefix _Dame_, to their forenames.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-35) Wives of Knights may prefix _Lady_ to their surnames, but no equivalent privilege exists for husbands of Knights or spouses of Dames. Such forms are not used by peers and princes, except when the names of the former are written out in their fullest forms. Male clergy of the [Church of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England "Church of England") and the [Church of Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Scotland "Church of Scotland") do not use the title _Sir_ (unless they were knighted before being ordained), as they do not receive the [accolade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accolade "Accolade") (they are not dubbed "knight" with a sword), although they do append the [post-nominal letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-nominal_letters "Post-nominal letters"); dames do not receive the accolade, and therefore female clergy are free to use the title _Dame_.

Knights and Dames Grand Cross use the post-nominal GBE; Knights Commander, KBE; Dames Commander, DBE; Commanders, CBE; Officers, OBE; and Members, MBE. The post-nominal for the British Empire Medal is BEM.

Members of all classes of the order are assigned positions in the [order of precedence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders_of_precedence_in_the_United_Kingdom "Orders of precedence in the United Kingdom"). Wives of male members of all classes also feature on the order of precedence, as do sons, daughters and daughters-in-law of Knights Grand Cross and Knights Commander; relatives of Ladies of the Order, however, are not assigned any special precedence. As a general rule, only wives and children of male recipients are afforded privileges.

Knights and Dames Grand Cross are also entitled to be granted [heraldic supporters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supporters_(heraldry) "Supporters (heraldry)"). They may, furthermore, encircle their arms with a depiction of the [circlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circlet "Circlet") (a circle bearing the motto) and the collar; the former is shown either outside or on top of the latter. Knights and Dames Commander and Commanders may display the circlet, but not the collar, surrounding their arms. The badge is depicted suspended from the collar or circlet.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-36)

## Forfeiture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Forfeiture")]

Only the monarch can annul an honour, based on recommendations from the [Honours Forfeiture Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honours_Forfeiture_Committee "Honours Forfeiture Committee"), which considers cases such as criminal convictions or actions that bring the honours system into disrepute. An individual can symbolically renounce their honour by returning the insignia to Buckingham Palace and ceasing to reference their title. However, the honour remains officially held unless formally annulled by the monarch.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-37)

For instance, [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") returned his MBE insignia in 1969 as a form of protest, but the honour was not formally annulled and remained officially in place.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-38)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-39)

## People who declined Order of the British Empire honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: People who declined Order of the British Empire honours")]

See also: [List of people who have declined a British honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_people_who_have_declined_a_British_honour "List of people who have declined a British honour")

In 2003, _[The Sunday Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sunday\_Times "The Sunday Times")_ published a list of the people who had rejected the Order of the British Empire, including [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), [John Cleese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cleese "John Cleese"), [Nigella Lawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigella_Lawson "Nigella Lawson"), [Elgar Howarth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgar_Howarth "Elgar Howarth"), [L. S. Lowry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._S._Lowry "L. S. Lowry"), [George Melly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Melly "George Melly"), and [J. G. Ballard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._G._Ballard "J. G. Ballard").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-mcgavin-40) In addition, Ballard voiced his opposition to the honours system, calling it "a preposterous charade".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-mcgavin-40)

The order has attracted some criticism for its naming having a connection with the idea of the now-extinct [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-FifthReport-41)[Benjamin Zephaniah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Zephaniah "Benjamin Zephaniah"), a British poet of [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Jamaicans "British Jamaicans") and [Barbadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbadian_British "Barbadian British") descent, publicly rejected appointment as an Officer in 2003 because, he asserted that the word "empire" reminded him of "thousands of years of brutality – it reminds me of how my foremothers were raped and my forefathers brutalised".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-42)

The author [C. S. Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._S._Lewis "C. S. Lewis") (1898–1963) was named on the last list of honours by [George VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_VI "George VI") in December 1951. Despite being a [monarchist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchist "Monarchist"), he declined in order to avoid association with any political issues.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-43)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-Letters_of_C.S._Lewis-44)

In 2019, comedian [John Oliver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Oliver "John Oliver") turned down an offer of appointment as an OBE, which would have been part of the [Queen's New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_New_Year_Honours "2020 New Year Honours") list, later saying: "Why on Earth would I want that?".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-45)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-46)

The members of the rock band [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") were appointed Members in 1965. [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") justified his investiture by comparing military membership in the Order: "Lots of people who complained about us receiving the MBE [status] received theirs for heroism in the war – for killing people ... We received ours for entertaining other people. I'd say we deserve ours more". Lennon later returned his MBE insignia on 25 November 1969, as part of his ongoing peace protests.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-47)

Other criticism centres on the view that many recipients of the Order are being rewarded with honours for simply doing their jobs; critics say that the Civil Service and Judiciary receive far more orders and honours than leaders of other professions.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-FifthReport-41)

[Chin Peng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chin_Peng "Chin Peng"), a veteran guerrilla fighter of the [Malayan Peoples' Anti-Japanese Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayan_Peoples'_Anti-Japanese_Army "Malayan Peoples' Anti-Japanese Army"), was appointed as an Officer for his role in fighting against the [Japanese occupation of Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_Malaya "Japanese occupation of Malaya") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), in close co-operation with the British commando [Force 136](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_136#Malayan_Communist_Party "Force 136"). Several years after the war, his OBE membership was withdrawn by the British government (and became undesirable to Chin Peng himself) when the Communist leader headed his party's guerrilla insurgency against the British Empire during the [Malayan Emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayan_Emergency "Malayan Emergency").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_note-48)

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Order_of_the_British_Empire&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Notes")]

1.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_ref-7 "Jump up")It is commonly written without "of the Most Excellent Order" and other words not implied by the post-nominals.
2.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_ref-15 "Jump up")Queen Mary, however, stipulated that the riband of a military Dame Grand Cross should not have a central grey stripe; the last appointment of a Dame Grand Cross in the military division was that of Dame [Sidney Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Browne "Sidney Browne") in 1919.
3.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_ref-19 "Jump up")Use of the BEM continued elsewhere in the Commonwealth; in the UK the BEM (civil) was restored to use 2012.
4.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_ref-25 "Jump up")Whereas DBE is the lowest rank of damehood, KBE is the second-lowest rank of knighthood (above [Knights Bachelor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Bachelor "Knights Bachelor")). Because of this, women are usually appointed DBE in circumstances when a man would be created a Knight Bachelor (for example, by convention, female judges of the [High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Justice "High Court of Justice") are created Dames Commander on appointment, while male judges become Knights Bachelor).
5.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire#cite_ref-35 "Jump up")Never surnames – thus Sir [Antony Sher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Sher "Antony Sher") may be shortened to Sir Antony, but not to Sir Sher.

_**Children of Men**_ is a 2006 [dystopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utopian_and_dystopian_fiction "Utopian and dystopian fiction")[action thriller film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action-thriller_film "Action-thriller film")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-7) directed and co-written by [Alfonso Cuarón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Cuar%C3%B3n "Alfonso Cuarón"). The screenplay, based on [P. D. James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._D._James "P. D. James")' 1992 novel _[The Children of Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Children\_of\_Men "The Children of Men")_, was credited to five writers, with [Clive Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Owen "Clive Owen") making additional, uncredited contributions. The film is set in 2027, when two decades of [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human "Human")[infertility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infertility "Infertility") have left human civilisation on the brink of collapse. [Asylum seekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asylum_seeker "Asylum seeker") seek sanctuary in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), where they are subjected to detention, deportation and execution by the government. Owen plays civil servant Theo Faron, who tries to help refugee Kee ([Clare-Hope Ashitey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clare-Hope_Ashitey "Clare-Hope Ashitey")) escape the chaos. _Children of Men_ also stars [Julianne Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julianne_Moore "Julianne Moore"), [Chiwetel Ejiofor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiwetel_Ejiofor "Chiwetel Ejiofor"), [Pam Ferris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Ferris "Pam Ferris"), [Charlie Hunnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Hunnam "Charlie Hunnam"), and [Sir Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine").

The film was released by [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") on 22 September 2006, in the UK and on 25 December in the US. Despite a limited marketing campaign during awards season by the film's distributor,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-10)_Children of Men_ received critical acclaim and was recognized for its achievements in screenwriting, cinematography, art direction, and innovative [single-shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_take "Long take") action sequences. While it underperformed at the box office, it was nominated for three [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Academy_Awards "79th Academy Awards"): [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), and [Best Film Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Film_Editing "Academy Award for Best Film Editing"). It was also nominated for three [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_British_Academy_Film_Awards "60th British Academy Film Awards"), winning [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "BAFTA Award for Best Cinematography") and [Best Production Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Production_Design "BAFTA Award for Best Production Design"), and for three [Saturn Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Awards "Saturn Awards"), winning [Best Science Fiction Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Science_Fiction_Film "Saturn Award for Best Science Fiction Film").

The film has received enduring acclaim and has been frequently cited as one of the best dystopian films[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-11) and often lauded as one of the greatest films of the 2000s,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-12) and of the 21st century.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_Men#cite_note-13) It was voted 13th in a [BBC critics' poll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC's_100_Greatest_Films_of_the_21st_Century "BBC's 100 Greatest Films of the 21st Century") on the best films released between 2000 and 2016 by film critics from around the world.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Children_of_Men&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 2027, total human infertility has led to wars and global depression, pushing civilization to the brink of collapse as humanity faces extinction. The UK has transformed into a totalitarian police state in which asylum seekers are arrested and put in camps. Daily life is full of bombings, rationing, decay and propaganda. The populace mourns as they hear the news that the youngest person alive in the world is killed at age eighteen.

Theo Faron, a former activist turned cynical, depressed bureaucrat, is kidnapped by the Fishes, a militant refugee rights group led by Theo's estranged wife, Julian Taylor. The pair separated after their son's death in 2008. Julian offers Theo money to acquire transit papers from his cousin, the Minister of Arts, for a young refugee woman named Kee. Theo visits his cousin inside an elite mini-city within London where the powerful enjoy all the pleasures of the past. Theo obtains joint transit papers from his cousin, then tells Julian that he is willing to escort Kee himself in exchange for more money. Luke, a Fishes member, drives Theo, Kee, Julian, and Miriam towards [Canterbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury "Canterbury"), but they are ambushed and Julian is killed. After the rest escape, Luke kills two police officers that stop them.

At a farm safe house, Kee reveals to Theo that she is pregnant, making her the only known pregnant woman in the world. Julian intended to take her to the Human Project, a secret scientific research group in the [Azores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azores "Azores") dedicated to curing humanity's infertility. That night, Theo eavesdrops and learns that Luke and other Fishes orchestrated Julian's death, while also intending to kill Theo and use Kee's baby as their political tool. Theo orchestrates an escape for himself, Kee, and Miriam, a midwife, to the secluded hideaway of Jasper Palmer, a bohemian, old friend of Theo.

The group plans to reach the Human Project ship, the _Tomorrow_, that Julian had scheduled to arrive offshore at [Bexhill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bexhill-on-Sea "Bexhill-on-Sea"), a notorious refugee detention centre. Jasper arranges for Syd, an immigration officer to whom Jasper sells cannabis, to smuggle them into Bexhill as refugees, from where they can take a rowboat and rendezvous with the ship. The next day, the Fishes arrive at Jasper's hidden entrance, forcing the group to flee. Jasper stays behind to stall them and is murdered by Luke. At an abandoned school, Syd meets Theo, Kee, and Miriam, and helps them board a bus to the camp where Kee's water breaks; Miriam feigns mental illness as a distraction and is dragged off the bus.

In Bexhill, their contact Marichka, a [Romani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people "Romani people") woman, provides Theo and Kee a room, where Theo helps Kee give birth. The next day, Syd arrives to tell them that fighting has broken out between the military and refugees, and that the Fishes have infiltrated the camp. He reveals that Theo and Kee have a bounty on their heads and attempts to capture them. Marichka and Theo fight off Syd, and the group takes shelter with a kindly, elderly Russian couple.

As they're heading for the rowboat, the Fishes capture Kee and the baby. Luke initially tells Patric and others to spare the group, but once Kee and the baby are out of earshot, Luke tells Patric to kill the Russian couple and Theo. Patric shoots one of the two refugees, but is interrupted by an attack by soldiers. Theo flees and tracks Kee to an apartment building under heavy fire. Theo confronts Luke, who tells Theo "We need him," mistaking the baby for a boy; Theo corrects Luke, who says "I had a sister" before pleading for the child again and subsequently being killed in an explosion.

Awed by the sight of an actual baby, the soldiers and Fishes momentarily stop fighting to allow Theo, Kee and the baby to leave the battle before the violence immediately resumes. Marichka leads them to the rowboat but stays behind. As fighter jets bomb Bexhill, Theo and Kee row to the buoy rendezvous point. Theo reveals he had been shot, and teaches Kee how to burp her baby. Kee tells him she will name the baby girl Dylan, after Theo's and Julian's lost son. Theo smiles weakly, then loses consciousness as the _Tomorrow_ approaches. As the screen cuts to black, children's laughter is heard.
